subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should Azure Realtime Talk ship as an OpenAI-provider gateway-relay path using the current Azure GA endpoint/auth contract with API-key support first, and what Entra or managed-identity behavior is required before merge?
rationale: The code already has partial Azure deployment plumbing, but choosing the endpoint shape, redirect policy, API-key versus Entra requirements, and browser fallback behavior changes a credential boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: API-Key-First Gateway Relay
options.body: Implement the current Azure GPT Realtime gateway-relay path with server-side API-key support, constrained Azure endpoint/auth handling, diagnostics, docs, and live proof, leaving Entra as a follow-up unless the endpoint contract requires it.

options.title: Require Entra Before Shipping
options.body: Hold the feature until Microsoft Entra or managed-identity support is designed and validated alongside API-key support, reducing enterprise auth churn at the cost of delaying Azure Talk.

options.title: Defer Until Azure Live Capacity Exists
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause implementation until maintainers have a deployable Azure Realtime resource and quota for end-to-end proof.

recommendation.title: API-Key-First Gateway Relay
recommendation.body: Implement the current Azure GPT Realtime gateway-relay path with server-side API-key support, constrained Azure endpoint/auth handling, diagnostics, docs, and live proof, leaving Entra as a follow-up unless the endpoint contract requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest feature-history signal for the OpenAI realtime provider and native Talk routing surfaces that need the product/security choice.
